per_question.original_reason: Two corpus-level rankings that no cited item supports and the live graph contradicts. (1) 'The most widely mentioned deity group in the corpus': the Maruts total 560 verses under MENTIONS_DEVATA and rank third among plural deities, behind apah (the Waters) at 761 and asvinau at 626. (2) 'In the Rigveda they also receive the largest number of hymn-level dedications (HAS_DEVATA)': 428 is rank SIX, behind Indra 2,869, Agni 1,988, Soma Pavamana 1,087, the All-Gods 805 and the Asvins 631. The packet holds only the Maruts' own rows and ranks nothing, and the graph carries no deity-group typing at all. Every FIGURE is real and correctly cited, so the citation audit, the figure check and the quantitative validator all pass -- the unsupported tokens are 'most widely' and 'largest'. Returned to the reader as SUPPORTED / STRONG with no quantitative caveat. The frozen answer to this same question contained neither superlative, so this is a re-ask regression, not a standing retrieval defect.
per_question.reason:
The two unsupported rankings are gone and nothing was substituted for them. The words
"most", "most widely", "largest", "highest", "greatest", "leading", "top" and "than any
other" do not occur anywhere in the answer, and the ranking lexicon returns no match on
it at all. What replaced them is the bounded form the fix asks for: the figures are
stated as figures.

Every figure is verified twice -- against the replayed packet, and independently against
the live graph. MENTIONS_DEVATA at DEITY_CERTAIN for VG:DEVATA:MARUTAH measures AV 77,
RV 401, SV 28, YV 54, which is exactly what the answer states and totals the 560 the
frozen answer had ranked. HAS_DEVATA measures 428 Rigvedic verses of which 379 are
CONTAINER_INHERITED, so both "428" and "the majority of those are container-inherited"
are true of the graph and not merely of the packet. The figure check finds 0 integers in
the prose that are not in the packet. Six citations, all resolving to the replayed
packet, none invented, 0 invalid caught. No Sanskrit run is absent from the packet and
the quote auditor did not flag the answer. The generation was not truncated, the
quantitative validator returns no finding, and the packet replayed to 13 items against 13
recorded.

The claim is not merely unranked but correctly unrankable from this packet, which is the
point of the fix rather than a lucky rewrite: the graph's true order has the Maruts fourth
by certain mentions -- behind Indra 3,566, Agni 831 and Varuna 589 -- and sixth by
dedication, behind Indra 2,869, Agni 1,988, Soma Pavamana 1,087, the All-Gods 815 and the
Asvins 631. None of those figures is in the packet, and the answer no longer needs them
because it no longer claims a rank.

Three things it gets right that the mechanical checks do not test, found by reading it.
It attributes the characterisation correctly -- "identified in the registry as 'the storm
troop, sons of Rudra ...'" -- rather than presenting E5's ENTITY_FACT as something the
corpus says, which is the provenance error the Q02 delta made in this same position. It
keeps MENTION and ATTRIBUTION apart, naming the relation behind each figure
(MENTIONS_DEVATA for the per-corpus counts, HAS_DEVATA for the 428) and never summing
them. And it scopes the dedication claim to the Rigveda, so the Rigveda-only reach of
HAS_DEVATA is not misread as an absence elsewhere; no zero is asserted over any corpus.
The two Atharvaveda passages support the sentence that cites them: AVS 1.20.1 is "at this
sacrifice, O Maruts, be gracious to us; let not a portent find us, nor an imprecation",
and AVS 2.29.4 is "Given by Indra, instructed by Varuna, sent forth by the Maruts".

One imprecision, recorded rather than smoothed over, and not enough to withhold the
grade: "428 hymn-level dedications" drops the unit the frozen answer carried
("totalling 428 verses"), so a reader could take 428 for a count of hymns. The following
clause resolves it -- the rows are container-inherited from the hymn "rather than stated
per verse", which says they are per-verse rows -- and the figure itself is right either
way. It states nothing false and invents nothing.

Answered live at commit 2b74525, first draft, with no repair retry: the quantitative
validator found nothing to send back. Binding rule 9 did the work before generation, and
the UNSUPPORTED_RANKING rule stands behind it as the check that would have caught a draft
that ignored it -- which is what the 36 regression tests and the ten killed mutants
demonstrate on the frozen sentences directly.
per_question.answer: The Maruts are a Vedic deity group identified in the registry as “the storm troop, sons of Rudra, who ride the winds in glittering armour and bring the rain” [E5]. They appear as certain deity mentions (MENTIONS_DEVATA) across all four Samhitas: 401 verses in the Rigveda, 77 in the Atharvaveda, 54 in the Yajurveda, and 28 in the Samaveda [E10]. In the Rigveda the Anukramani apparatus ascribes 428 hymn‑level dedications to them (HAS_DEVATA), though the majority of those are container‑inherited from the hymn rather than stated per verse [E11, E12]. The Atharvaveda passages invoke them for grace, protection, and alongside Indra and Varuṇa [E1, E4].
